en.27:45: From the sixth hour until the ninth hour darkness came over all the land.
en.27:46: About the ninth hour Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?” which means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”
en.27:47: When some of those standing there heard this, they said, “He is calling Elijah.”
en.27:48: One of them quickly ran and brought a sponge. He filled it with sour wine, put it on a reed, and held it up for Jesus to drink.
en.27:49: But the others said, “Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to save Him.”
en.27:50: When Jesus had cried out again in a loud voice, He yielded up His spirit.
en.27:51: At that moment the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom. The earth quaked, and the rocks were split.
en.27:52: The tombs broke open, and the bodies of many saints who had fallen asleep were raised.
en.27:53: After Jesus’ resurrection, when they had come out of the tombs, they entered the holy city and appeared to many people.
en.27:54: When the centurion and those with him who were guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and all that had happened, they were terrified and said, “Truly this was the Son of God.”
en.27:55: And many women were there, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus from Galilee to minister to Him.
en.27:56: Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee’s sons.

en.15:33: From the sixth hour until the ninth hour darkness came over all the land.
en.15:34: At the ninth hour, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”
en.15:35: When some of those standing nearby heard this, they said, “Behold, He is calling Elijah.”
en.15:36: And someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine. He put it on a reed and held it up for Jesus to drink, saying, “Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to take Him down.”
en.15:37: But Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed His last.
en.15:38: And the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
en.15:39: When the centurion standing there in front of Jesus saw how He had breathed His last, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!”
en.15:40: And there were also women watching from a distance. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.
en.15:41: These women had followed Jesus and ministered to Him while He was in Galilee, and there were many other women who had come up to Jerusalem with Him.

en.23:44: It was now about the sixth hour, and darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour.
en.23:45: The sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn down the middle.
en.23:46: Then Jesus called out in a loud voice, “Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit.” And when He had said this, He breathed His last.
en.23:47: When the centurion saw what had happened, he gave glory to God, saying, “Surely this was a righteous man.”
en.23:48: And when all the people who had gathered for this spectacle saw what had happened, they returned home beating their breasts.
en.23:49: But all those who knew Jesus, including the women who had followed Him from Galilee, stood at a distance watching these things.

en.19:28: After this, knowing that everything had now been accomplished, and to fulfill the Scripture, Jesus said, “I am thirsty.”
en.19:29: A jar of sour wine was sitting there. So they soaked a sponge in the wine, put it on a stalk of hyssop, and lifted it to His mouth.
en.19:30: When Jesus had received the sour wine, He said, “It is finished.” And bowing His head, He yielded up His spirit.
en.19:31: It was the day of Preparation, and the next day was a High Sabbath. In order that the bodies would not remain on the cross during the Sabbath, the Jews asked Pilate to have the legs broken and the bodies removed.
en.19:32: So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man who had been crucified with Jesus, and those of the other.
en.19:33: But when they came to Jesus and saw that He was already dead, they did not break His legs.
en.19:34: Instead, one of the soldiers pierced His side with a spear, and immediately blood and water flowed out.
en.19:35: The one who saw it has testified to this, and his testimony is true. He knows that he is telling the truth, so that you also may believe.
en.19:36: Now these things happened so that the Scripture would be fulfilled: “Not one of His bones will be broken.”
en.19:37: And, as another Scripture says: “They will look on the One they have pierced.”
